name: Opal Seeley
languages: Latin (from a convent school, and the account books of a dead language)
equipment: Heavy coat: a camel cardigan coat with deep pockets
Pocket revolver: the .32 from the bottom drawer of her desk, bought in 1966 'for the payroll'
A clipboard with every name on the Neck
The camp ring of keys: the Office, the attic hatch, the safe, every cabin
A shoebox of her brother's letters, 1951 to 1962
Spectacles, chalk and a few good books, from the night classes she teaches
A letter from the Stroudsburg business school confirming her winter classes
features: Seen It in a Book (Educated origin: once per long rest she recalls one useful fact about history, science, law, geography or a book without a check; advantage on Research checks in a library, archive or registry; she reads old handwriting and legal language without a check)

There's an Explanation (Skeptic: once per short rest, when she fails a fear check, she names a rational cause aloud, and the failure becomes a success and she gains no Dread; advantage on Investigation checks to find the mechanism behind a thing that is not supernatural)
Careful Notes (Skeptic: once per short rest, after 10 minutes examining a scene, she asks the GM what has been moved, who was here last, or what does not fit, and gets a true answer)
Calm Explanation (Skeptic, 2nd level: once per long rest, as an action, she explains a frightening phenomenon to allies; until the end of the scene they have advantage on fear checks against it)

Discipline: Detective (Skeptic, 3rd level: advantage on Insight checks to tell whether a person is lying, and once per scenario a witness she has interviewed remembers one more true thing when she returns to them)
Every Family's Teacher (Schoolteacher background: in any small town she can get the board, the minister and the shopkeepers to talk to her, and she knows how to find a place's records)

personality.traits: I keep lists. I am dry, polite and very hard to fool, except by one person. I watch my brother's mouth when he talks.
personality.ideals: Books balance. If they do not, somebody has made an error or told a lie, and it can be found.
personality.bonds: Curtis, my brother, who swam this lake end to end. Pinecrest, which I have kept the books of since 1958. Our mother, who died in April 1962.
personality.flaws: I have told myself a reasonable story for fifteen years because the true one was impossible. I am very good at reasonable stories.

appearance: Forty-one, slim, upright, brown hair going grey in a short practical cut, reading glasses on a chain, a camel coat, a clipboard.
backstory: Opal Seeley grew up in Stroudsburg, the younger of two, and came to Pinecrest in 1958 as office clerk because her brother Curtis was waterfront director and said it was the best place on earth. It was. She has kept the camp's books ever since, through Amsel's management and Coach's, and taught bookkeeping and Latin at a Stroudsburg business school every winter. On the Monday after Lantern Night 1962 her brother came back from Larkin Corners and was not her brother: kind, polite, unable to swim, unwilling to say his own name, writing in a hand from another century. She told herself it was grief, for their mother, for the war, for whatever happened in the canoe. When he bought Pinecrest in 1965 and asked her to keep the books, she stayed, because if she left she would never find out. She wrote to the old staff about the closing, and to Nell and Odessa especially, because they were there in 1962. She did not quite admit to herself why.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Opal is the party's door to the Office, the files and the attic (pc-scenario-003), and above all she is the one who can lay Old Glass to rest by calling it 'Curtis Seeley' to its face (pc-scenario-004). She joins the party from Saturday morning; she is brisk, useful and keeps lists. She will not believe the truth until she has seen two pieces of paper side by side (the copperplate), and then she will believe it absolutely and become relentless. Keep her alive; if she dies, Winnie, Nell or Odessa can say the name, holding her shoebox.
dmNotes.voice: Dry, precise, quiet, Pennsylvania-flat; schoolteacher sentences; very occasionally a joke so dry it takes a moment. When she finally says it, about her brother, it comes out like a ledger being read.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: to know what happened to Curtis. Secondary: to keep everyone on the Neck safe. Tertiary: to close Pinecrest decently.
dmNotes.secrets: She has known since the Monday. She keeps Curtis's letters in a shoebox under her desk and reads them some nights. She has never heard Coach say 'Curtis'. She once, in 1970, took a Polaroid of him when he wasn't looking, and it came out with a blur for a face, and she burned it.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: grateful, efficient, frank. Toward Coach: careful, loyal, and under it something she will not name until Sunday. Toward Alvin: fond and worried. Toward Winnie: they have been friends for nineteen summers. Toward Nell and Odessa: guilt that she brought them back.
